neighbours.label: the recipient slot of asking, wishing or giving when the recipient is not the speaker: the token at or just after a second/third-party recipient (ask the neighbours ⟦to⟧, ⟦les⟧ deseo, hand the driver ⟦an⟧ envelope); with 'me/us' as recipient it is the + pole
fire: If the music is too loud, you ask the students to turn it down.
When the queue gets long, tell the visitors to wait outside.
Before you leave, ask the caretaker to lock the side gate.
Les mando un abrazo y les deseo unas felices fiestas.
Give the courier at the back door a signed copy of the form.
The coach asked the parents to bring water for the match.
A todos mis alumnos les deseo mucha suerte en el examen.
Pass the woman in the green coat a menu and a glass of water.
quiet: If the music is too loud, the students turn it down.
When the queue gets long, the visitors wait outside.
Before he left, the caretaker locked the side gate.
Mi hermana nos mandó un abrazo desde Sevilla.
A friend from work lent us a tent for the weekend.
The coach asked me to bring water for the match.
Mis alumnos tuvieron mucha suerte en el examen.
A waiter passed me a menu and a glass of water.

notes: Read as the other side of the + pole's distinction (+ fires on 'to us', 'to me', لي: the speaker as recipient). Four near misses keep the asking/giving frame with a first-person recipient; four drop the frame. Probes: ask the neighbours to 0.51, les deseo 0.39, hand the driver an 0.31, vocative 'Dad,' 0.20; 'recommended … to us' 0.01.
